title: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites
slides: Satlyt raises $8M, but can it make satellites think?
Founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager.
The AI runs on satellites, not in distant data centers.
Data processed in orbit, cutting delays and bandwidth costs.
Test one satellite image yourself; see what changes.
thread_text:
1. $8M for satellite AI

Satlyt just raised $8M to put AI directly on satellites. The goal: process images in orbit instead of sending them to Earth.

2. From Google to orbit

Founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager. That mix of big tech and rocket science is rare.

3. No data center needed

The AI runs on the satellite itself. No distant servers, no waiting for data to travel.

4. Faster and cheaper

Processing in orbit cuts delays and bandwidth costs. That changes what satellites can do in real time.

5. Test it yourself

Find a satellite image and imagine AI analyzing it instantly. Would that change how you use the data?

instagram.caption:
Eight million dollars just went to making satellites process their own images, instead of shipping every pixel down to Earth.

Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, is putting AI directly on satellites.

That means images get analyzed in orbit, cutting delays and bandwidth costs.

If you work with satellite imagery, your data could arrive already interpreted, not raw.

🛰️ Faster than waiting on a downlink 📡

What would you do differently if the analysis came back in seconds?
